Closes #279

## Summary

Bind each transfer to the quote the sender reviewed, and refuse confirmation when the quote, wallet connection, connectivity, or available balance cannot support it. This includes the original quote-freshness work and the subsequent locale, balance, and pending-connection corrections.

## Changes

- quoteBinding validates currency pairs, fingerprints priced inputs, checks signability, and reconciles canonical amounts. buildQuote adds a deterministic quote ID, fx.table source, and input fingerprint.
- QuoteCard displays quote source, ID, timestamps, expiry, and currency precision, with an explicit refresh action.
- SendMoney invalidates confirmation on priced-input and network changes, blocks expired quotes, and saves the reviewed quoteId in the transfer payload.
- French keyboard review parses localized input before canonical comparison. Portuguese repeated blur preserves the decimal separator. Canonical balance values are compared without parsing them through the input locale again.
- Confirmation requires the actual account returned by connect() and checks the bound amount against that account's balance. Rejected/incomplete connections and newly connected insufficient balances stop before transfer creation; affordable and exact-balance transfers remain supported.
- A confirmation version changes when its quote is invalidated or refreshed. After awaiting wallet connection, a superseded confirmation stops before transfer creation, including when connectivity drops and recovers during the wait. A live connectivity check also blocks current offline submission. The submission lock and finally release remain.
- Correct null-price feedback for an otherwise valid amount, update the four maintained test files to exercise the actual confirmation/result flow and canonical decimal contract, and apply the existing formatter to its fifteen flagged files. Exact money, offline blocking, submission lock, retry, receipt reconciliation, and no-create assertions remain.

## Compatibility and tradeoffs

Quote id/source and Transfer quoteId are additive; legacy records still parse. Identical priced inputs and clock produce the same quote ID; a later refresh produces a new one. Before dispatch, a network interruption clears the pending quote and requires a new review. Already-dispatched transfers retain their existing result handling.

Closes #65

## Summary

Enforce position ownership at the service boundary and bind HTTP callers to server-provisioned identities. Forged wallet or role headers cannot disclose or mutate another user's positions. The authenticated routes also return valid v1 transaction receipts: authorized deposits return 201, and withdrawals and transaction history return 200.

This description covers the original position policy, the credential implementation, and the composed receipt correction at current head [`30457194`](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/YieldVault-Backend-1/commit/3045719435ee12f89018151d735c14b9de2000b8).

## Position access

- Every `/api/positions` route and `GET /api/vaults/:id/positions` requires an opaque Bearer token. `POSITION_CREDENTIALS` maps its SHA-256 digest to an exact subject and role; `X-Wallet-Address` and `X-Audit-Role` carry no position-access authority.
- Controllers pass the authenticated actor and operator binding into the shared `src/auth/positionAccess.js` service policy. Ordinary users see their own positions; missing and foreign IDs return the same 404 (`Position not found`), and cross-user list or summary filters return empty results. Malformed IDs also fail closed. A caller-selected body user cannot authorize a mutation.
- The existing `admin` and `auditor` policy remains: configured operators can inspect other positions and act for an explicit target user. Trusted in-process service callers retain their explicit-user interface; unscoped dumps remain forbidden.
- Missing, malformed, unknown or unconfigured credentials receive 401 and a Bearer challenge before position handling. Protected responses include `Cache-Control: private, no-store`.

## Credential configuration and rollout

The dependency-free verifier accepts at most 100 immutable `{subject, role, tokenSha256}` entries. Subjects are bounded, trimmed identifiers without C0/C1 controls; roles are lowercase identifiers and digests must be unique. Malformed configuration stops startup without echoing its contents, and an empty registry denies position access. Verification compares every configured digest; the compiled registry does not retain raw tokens.

[README configuration and migration instructions](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/YieldVault-Backend-1/blob/3045719435ee12f89018151d735c14b9de2000b8/README.md#position-credentials) cover token generation, replacing header-only clients, and restart-based rotation and revocation. Credentials have no automatic expiry. This authenticates provisioned identities for the in-memory mock service; it does not prove control of a Stellar wallet. Public vault metadata and unrelated routes retain their existing access rules. No data migration is needed for the in-memory store.

## Valid v1 transaction receipts

The integration preserves both the authentication history at [`fcb73610`](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/YieldVault-Backend-1/commit/fcb73610d3252b61280a279df7c49b617d17e703) and the existing serializer repair at [`e45ca72d`](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/YieldVault-Backend-1/commit/e45ca72d87e0d0749e4a1e4d4ff87242cb8e6cbb). The serializer maps the mock provider's exact `SUCCESS` value to the v1 `confirmed` state and omits provider-only `network` and `ledger` fields from HTTP responses. Stored provider receipts and lifecycle records keep their original values.

Other fields still pass through the strict response validator, including unknown-field, unsupported-state, amount-precision and required-field checks. Position-controller composition preserves the authenticated `accessFrom(req)` bindings. Full withdrawal returns a null position. The previous post-write HTTP 500 caused by the receipt/response-contract mismatch is resolved.

## Current validation

Tested integration: [`e5ac9060f1fd771f1a91b89ad6c55823b9dcfef7`](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/YieldVault-Backend-1/commit/e5ac9060f1fd771f1a91b89ad6c55823b9dcfef7). Current head `30457194` adds the source-bound report without changing that product source.

One completed [native job](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/RemitFlow-Backend/actions/runs/37193117137/job/111409297443) ran on Ubuntu 24.04.5 with Node 22.23.3. Its workflow is hosted in the RemitFlow-Backend fork and explicitly checks out this YieldVault repository at `e5ac9060`.

- The same 17 contract cases reproduce **13 passes / 4 failures** on parent production `fcb73610` and **17 passes** on the integration.
- `npm test -- --test-concurrency=1`: **150 passed, zero failed or skipped**. This includes the unchanged 21-case ownership/HTTP suite and eight credential-helper cases, covering spoofed-header and unauthorized-mutation denials.
- `npm run validate:contracts`: all **eight unchanged response fixtures** validated.

| Actual application request | Parent | Integration |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Authorized deposit | 500 | 201 |
| Authorized partial withdrawal | 500 | 200 |
| Authorized full withdrawal | 500 | 200 |
| First transaction-history page | 500 | 200 |
| Next transaction-history page | Not reached after first-page failure | 200 |

These requests use the actual Express application, Bearer middleware and in-memory mock provider. The reused fixture provisions a fresh opaque credential for its synthetic subject and restores configuration after each case. Successful mutations also check the stored receipt and confirmed lifecycle state.

[Committed report, source identities and reproduction](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/YieldVault-Backend-1/blob/3045719435ee12f89018151d735c14b9de2000b8/docs/AUTHENTICATED_V1_RECEIPTS.md) links the exact workflow and baseline/candidate output artifact. The unchanged manifest resolved Express 4.22.3, cors 2.8.6, dotenv 16.6.1, morgan 1.12.1 and uuid 9.0.1; this branch has no dependency lockfile.

## Validation boundary

The earlier credential implementation's execution remains tied to `fcb73610`; the results above establish its composition with the receipt correction at `e5ac9060`. The original credential, policy, provider, accounting, lifecycle, schema and fixture files are unchanged by that composition.

Validation covers the local mock service. Live wallets, Stellar transactions, frontend browser sessions and production deployment were not exercised. The linked passing job is the source-pinned validation carrier; it does not establish the state of the sponsor repository's separate workflow or maintainer acceptance.

Closes #278

## Summary

Transfer history paging now uses a filter-scoped snapshot with cursor tie-breakers so new transfers arriving mid-scroll cannot duplicate or omit rows. Filter changes reset the snapshot; expired cursors recover cleanly.

## What changed

- **`transferSnapshot`** builds a frozen membership list sorted by `createdAt` desc with `id` as the stable tie-breaker, encodes scoped cursors, and recovers when a cursor is expired or out of scope.
- **`Transfers`** pages against the snapshot instead of a live offset slice. Concurrent inserts stay off the current pages until filters reset or the snapshot TTL elapses.
- Empty snapshots created while the list is still loading are rebuilt once rows arrive (so first paint is not frozen empty).

## Tradeoffs

- Snapshot TTL is five minutes — long enough for a paging session, short enough that a stale view does not linger forever.
- Pull-to-refresh updates live record fields for snapshotted ids but does not reshuffle membership mid-page; that is intentional.

## Compatibility

- UI-only change to pagination mechanics; filter URL sync and selection toolbar behavior are preserved.
- Existing filter / select-all suites remain green.

arguments.body:
Closes #278

## Summary

Transfer history uses a filter-scoped snapshot so concurrent inserts cannot duplicate or omit rows while paging. This continuation fixes recovery and selection behavior, prepares sort keys once, and repairs existing CI fixtures.

## Behavior and compatibility

- Freeze filtered membership in descending creation-time order with locale-aware ID ties and stable equal-key order. Keep every matching row, with five rows per page; no result cap or cache is introduced.
- Bind cursors to the snapshot generation, filter scope and prior row key. Expired, malformed or out-of-scope cursors recover to a fresh first page. Snapshots expire after five minutes; filter changes reset them, and empty snapshots rebuild when loading supplies rows.
- Mint distinct in-memory generation IDs even when replacement snapshots share a clock tick, filter and row count. An old cursor cannot alias that replacement.
- Refresh existing members' live fields without reshuffling membership, including when their fields cease matching the filter. Retain captured records for vanished rows; new inserts appear in the next snapshot.
- Clear explicit selections and select-all when filters change or a persisted snapshot generation is replaced. Preserve selection during same-generation refresh. URL filters and pagination controls remain compatible.
- Keep the maintained review/confirmation/result/receipt flow and canonical decimal assertions. Offline blocking, retry, exactly-once creation and money checks remain. A valid amount that cannot be priced now receives the pricing explanation.

## Snapshot performance

The sorter prepares timestamp/string-ID keys once per populated row and returns the original row references. It preserves locale ties, invalid-date fallback and undefined/sparse placement.

Measured calls to the actual snapshot constructor include record copying: Node 22.16.0, two warmups and five alternating paired samples per workload, with complete output equality:

- 5,000 shuffled: 20.349 → 3.071 ms (6.63x).
- 100,000 shuffled: 620.098 → 80.338 ms (7.72x).
- 100,000 oldest-first: 37.541 → 28.876 ms (1.30x).

Separate untimed counting measured 3,058,470 → 100,000 timestamp parses for the large shuffled case. The tradeoff is one temporary key record per populated row; peak memory was not measured. Storage parsing, network/provider work and React rendering are excluded.

[Benchmark, raw samples, exact source pins and focused execution](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/RemitFlow-Frontend/blob/5ef95f76c2b77abd8458cbdbc3ca4582e4fad19c/docs/performance/snapshot-sort-20261004.md).

## Validation and current status

Current head: 1ee074a9deb2512b18437664dc74830f1e7f6bc0. Subsequent lookup, across-page selection, and inactive-date-filter changes retain their source-specific evidence below.

- Earlier full selection: source 157ff7bffe98c96ad48b39c844ff51a0a070679a passed 477 tests across 49 files, with zero failed/pending/todo/skipped. Node 24.19.0 / Vitest 4.1.10; 56.57 s reported, 57.113 s process. Existing formatting and production build passed (1.55 s Vite). All 344 tracked files stayed unchanged after execution.
- Later sorter validation: source 2ae93359afb19092961f328377955106259251d4 passed 13 focused tests, zero failed/skipped, in 1.53 s; changed JavaScript passed Prettier and the production build passed (917 ms Vite), on Node 22.23.3. Those tested sorter bytes are retained in the current head. The earlier 477-test aggregate was not rerun or relabeled as a current whole-suite result.
- Dated critical audit: the 4 October 2026, 11:56 UTC receipt exited 0 with 0 critical / 20 high / 12 moderate / 2 low. It is reused for identical package/lock bytes; remaining findings are not claimed repaired.

[Aggregate commands, receipt and raw evidence](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/RemitFlow-Frontend/blob/409bc61215bc8ff7e76b4ce48b4787c0160997d7/docs/validation/rf297-existing-gates-20261004/README.md). Hosted [CI](https://github.com/RemitFlow/RemitFlow-Frontend/actions/runs/37201968643) and [Lighthouse](https://github.com/RemitFlow/RemitFlow-Frontend/actions/runs/37201968593) require approval; maintainer acceptance remains pending.

## Page lookup continuations

At [3bb8747d](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/RemitFlow-Frontend/commit/3bb8747d62c1e9690f9a1559c7f6d73f792bd9d1), page lookups retain only visible snapshot IDs rather than allocating a full-history Map and temporary pairs for each page. The lookup preserves the last duplicate-ID winner, exact live references and captured-record fallback for missing rows, with no persistent cache. Direct production-module measurement on Node 22.16/Linux: 100,000 rows with the default five-row page measured 14.269 → 1.606 ms median (8.89x); lookup cardinality fell from 100,000 to 5. Complete outputs and references matched across bounded mutation, insertion, duplicate, expiry and scope observations. [Source pins, all four workloads, raw samples and runnable measurement](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/RemitFlow-Frontend/blob/3bb8747d62c1e9690f9a1559c7f6d73f792bd9d1/docs/performance/snapshot-page-lookup-20261004.md).

Subsequent source [afa3b0ef](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/RemitFlow-Frontend/commit/afa3b0efb5c7e0bd2eee2e6123c1206e7c801ac8) retains the bounded page map and avoids unnecessary live-history traversal. Ordinary arrays are scanned backward so the first match preserves the last-duplicate-wins policy; scanning stops after every visible ID is resolved. Empty pages read no live records. Missing IDs retain their snapshot fallback after a full scan. Sets, generators and custom array iterators keep their forward-only behavior.

Three focused assertion groups passed against the complete production module, and all six benchmark workload outputs and record references matched the preceding source. On Node 22.16, the 100,000-row ascending-input newest page measured 2.793942 → 0.007302 ms, and an empty filtered snapshot 1.590464 → 0.002271 ms. Full-scan controls were essentially unchanged: descending first page 2.754172 → 2.726743 ms; ascending last page 2.798958 → 2.804947 ms. Nine alternating pairs, twenty calls per sample. [Source pins, reproduction program, raw samples and limits](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/RemitFlow-Frontend/blob/afa3b0efb5c7e0bd2eee2e6123c1206e7c801ac8/docs/performance/snapshot-early-stop-20261004/README.md).

These results depend on input position and measure only the helper. Prior benchmark ratios must not be multiplied; no browser, provider or whole-application speedup is claimed. No Vitest suite, build or workflow was rerun for either lookup continuation; earlier validation remains source-specific. Maintainer acceptance remains pending.

## Across-page deselection

Across-page deselection now converts the frozen membership to explicit IDs before removing a row or page, so other-page selections survive. The maintained selection integration file passes all five cases with no skipped cases on Node 24.21.0 and unchanged locked dependencies at production source [6ed4086f](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/RemitFlow-Frontend/commit/6ed4086fa9520c36639b5419a42145951a16cd9a); both new cases fail against the preceding component. Scoped formatting and source-identity checks pass. [Execution and limits](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/RemitFlow-Frontend/blob/521ef150b7da2a0d93bebfd9537a5ce1c9d2897f/docs/validation/across-page-deselection.md).

## Inactive date filter

At production source [9f1debe8](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/RemitFlow-Frontend/commit/9f1debe8fb5ba5f79fc6fe83349d4264faa7b13b), the All time filter defers its default Date allocation until a nonzero date range needs it. Supplied clocks, inclusive cutoffs, invalid dates and active ranges keep their behavior. Previous selection and pagination changes remain.

A native Node 22.16.0/Linux measurement of Array.filter calling the complete production helper over 100,000 records used three warmups and nine alternating paired samples. The All time median measured 12.115259 → 4.508355 ms (62.79% less time), with identical membership, order and object references; separate untimed clock allocations fell from 100,000 to zero. The active 30-day control measured 62.660949 → 60.724011 ms with 100,000 allocations in both implementations; that small difference is not treated as a material active-filter gain. Rendering, API and storage work are excluded.

[Native run 37206173166](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/RemitFlow-Frontend/actions/runs/37206173166) passes all eight unchanged transfers-filter integration cases at pinned source 9f1debe8, including no-filter display, date presets and URL restoration. The original lock is installed; scoped formatting and clean-worktree checks pass. No test file or dependency was added. [Source pins, raw samples, reproduction and limits](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/RemitFlow-Frontend/blob/1ee074a9deb2512b18437664dc74830f1e7f6bc0/docs/performance/date-range-clock.md).

These separate source-bound results are not combined into a current-head whole-suite total or a cumulative performance multiplier. No full build, deployed throughput, acceptance or payout is asserted for these continuations.

Closes #281

## Summary

Transfer search and filtering now use actor-scoped, debounced, cancellable queries with stable sort semantics and a hard result cap so large histories stay correct and responsive.

## What changed

- **`transferSearch` helpers** define canonical filter matching, newest-first sort with `id` tie-breaker, actor visibility (including legacy unscoped rows), query scope keys, and result capping (`DEFAULT_RESULT_CAP` / `MAX_RESULT_CAP`).
- **`listTransfers`** requires actor scope on every request, accepts search/status/range/limit, honours `AbortSignal`, and returns a stably sorted capped page.
- **`useTransfers`** aborts the previous in-flight list call when filters change and drops stale replies so a slow response cannot overwrite the active filter set.
- **`Transfers`** debounces free-text search before updating the URL and driving the query; status/range still apply immediately. Optional `actorId` on the Transfer contract is stamped on create and seeds.

## Tradeoffs

- Search URL updates after the debounce window (300ms) so keystrokes do not fan out requests; shareable links still settle on the committed term.
- Result lists are capped (default 100) so unbounded histories cannot stall the UI; callers can request up to `MAX_RESULT_CAP`.
- Legacy rows without `actorId` remain readable only under the demo actor during migration.

## Compatibility

- Additive optional `actorId` on Transfer; existing fixtures without it still load for the demo actor.
- Filter URL params (`search`, `status`, `range`) and pagination UI are unchanged.

## Test evidence

```text
npx vitest run \
  test/unit/transfer-search.test.js \
  test/unit/list-transfers-search.test.js \
  test/unit/useTransfers-search-race.test.jsx \
  test/unit/useTransfers.errors.test.jsx \
  test/integration/transfers-filter.test.jsx \
  test/integration/transfers-search-scale.test.jsx \
  test/integration/select-all-across-pages.test.jsx
# Test Files  7 passed | Tests  31 passed

npm run build  # ok
```

Coverage includes stale-response races, AbortSignal cancellation, actor scope isolation, result capping, pagination on a large fixture, and a 5k-row performance budget.

## Out of scope

- Broad rewrites, unrelated services, or cosmetic-only changes.

Closes #281

## Summary

Transfer search keeps actor scope, cancellation and stable capped results. This continuation fixes navigation and validation gaps, improves large-history selection, and closes local CI failures.

## Behavior and compatibility

- Restrict raw rows to the actor before validation. Foreign-wallet corruption cannot alter the current wallet's error behavior; malformed responses and corrupt visible records retain their validation policy.
- Abort superseded requests and reject stale replies. Typed search debounces for 300 ms; status/date changes apply immediately. URL navigation restores the corresponding search without a pending typed value overwriting it.
- Scan once, count every match and retain a bounded heap: default 100 rows, maximum 500. Preserve descending creation time, exact ID-string ordering, input order for equal keys, row identity and input immutability.
- Prepare status, folded search and date cutoff once per query; bypass empty filters. Rows and date windows stay fresh; no result cache is added. Inclusive boundaries and invalid/oversized windows retain their behavior.
- Repair four maintained fixtures to follow review, confirmation, result and receipt navigation and canonical decimal values. Preserve exact money, no-create, offline, submission-count and retry assertions. An otherwise valid amount with no price now receives the pricing explanation.

Actor identity is additive and stamped on creation. Legacy unscoped records remain visible only to the demo actor. URL parameters and pagination stay compatible. This is the localStorage demonstration API and mock wallet, not an external authorization or settlement service.

## Performance evidence

Bounded heap — Node 24.19.0. The 100,000-row shuffled case (100-row cap) measured 776.075 → 26.912 ms, 28.84x, with identical outputs/references. Separate untimed observations counted 3,031,310 → 100,000 timestamp parses and 100,000 → 100 sorted rows. These are medians of five alternating paired samples. [All four workloads, raw samples and exact source pins](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/RemitFlow-Frontend/blob/ecefe06d68ca6838434b755525cfc3cc6c701d4f/docs/performance/transfer-search-20261004/README.md).

Filter preparation — Node 22.23.3. Starting from that optimized heap, the 100,000-row date-window workload measured 77.677 → 41.512 ms (46.56% less time); combined filters measured 37.811 → 26.264 ms (30.54% less). This separate native run used three warmups and nine alternating pairs; outputs/references matched and 10,368 untimed compatibility comparisons passed. [All five workloads, executed selector f072d787, source pins and run](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/RemitFlow-Frontend/blob/71746fa5552f2dbb0ad3727637b52b9f64747410/docs/performance/transfer-filter-preparation-20261004/README.md).

These comparisons use different fixtures/runtimes and are not multiplied into a cumulative speedup. They measure the production selector, excluding storage decoding, validation, simulated API delay, rendering and providers. Both historical benchmarks are preserved without reruns; no whole-page latency or peak-memory claim is made.
